label: text

label: text
text: (Router's American Service.)

label: text
text:
MICHIGAN CITY, May 31.
"Strangler" Lewis, claimant for the world's heavyweight wrestling championship, threw Wayne Munn for two falls out of three by using a succession of headlocks.

label: text
text: Munn was carried from the ring. Lewis gets the bulk of the $30,000 purse and retains a $10,000 diamond belt.

label: paragraph_title

label: paragraph_title
text:
DUPRE AND JIM
CARTLIDGE.

label: text
text: Andre Dupre (ex-featherweight champion of France) is coming back to Hongkong and a return bout with C. P. O. Jim Cartlidge (undefeated Imperial Services champion and lightweight beltholder of the Colony) is practically certain.

label: text
text:
Mr. J. Brook, the popular manager of the Hongkong Boxing Association, has received a cable that Dupre is returning here by the P. & O. S.S. Nagoya. Mr. T. G. Bennett, the enthusiastic hon. secretary and treasurer of the Association, has lost no time in making a start with the preparations for another big fight.
Dupre, on his arrival, will undergo a special course of training under Staff Sergt. Hunt, the well-known physical culturist and gymnast.

label: text
text: Cartlidge will train at his old quarters at the Kowloon British School.

label: text
text: No date has yet been fixed for the bout, but doubtless this awaits the actual arrival of Dupre on the scene.

label: text
text: It is understood that Dupre has now arrived in the Colony and that hopes exist of bringing the men together on June 18

label: paragraph_title
text: NEW CHAMPION.

label: text
text: WORLD'S CRUISER WEIGHT TITLE

label: text
text: MCTIGUE DEFEATED.

label: text
text: SPLENDID RALLY IN LAST ROUND.

label: paragraph_title
text: (Reuter's American Service.)

label: text
text: Paul Berlenbach has been given decision over Mike McTigue, in light-heavyweight boxing championship of the world.

label: text
text: By defeating McTigue, Berlenbach becomes the fourth holder of the world's light-heavyweight title in three years.

label: text
text: Berlenbach was most aggressive. He repeatedly forced McTigue to the ropes and was boring in with hard rights and lefts but McTigue covered up and dodged causing Berlenbach frequently to miss. Nevertheless, Berlenbach landed in number of solid punches, cutting McTigue's eyes and mouth.

label: vision_footnote
text: The defeated champion.

label: text
text: McTigue rallied gamely in the final round and took the offensive but the judges had no difficulty in awarding Berlenbach the decision.

label: paragraph_title
text: MILITARY BOXING

label: text
text: SURREYS' PLATOON

label: text
text: "Tommies" Do Well

label: text
text: Bouts of three two-minute rounds under Service conditions were the order of things at Murray Barracks on Saturday night when the semi-finals and finals of the Surrey Regiment's platoon boxing tournament for the Montague Bates Cup were decided.

label: text
text: The three days' sport in the "Montague Bates" Platoon Boxing Tournament proved a success in every way, and those who went to witness the semi-finals and finals last night were treated to a display which was quite creditable in the realm of army boxing.

label: text
text: The best bout was easily the final of the bantamweight between Pte. Baxter and Drm. Simpson. Both men gave a splendid exhibition of clean boxing.

label: text
text: One bout in the semi-final of the flyweight and two in the welter-weights were not fought, one of the contentants in each case being indisposed, thus providing a walk-over for the others into the final. However, the latter gave exhibition fights with others who filled the gap.

label: text
text:
Five out of the seven final events went the full distance,
Owing to a misunderstanding in the awarding of points for the Cup, an adjustment had to be made, the results at the conclusion being as follows:—Drums and Signals, total points 10; Machine Guns (Right Section), total points 8½.

label: text
text: Results:—

label: paragraph_title
text: SEMI-FINALS.

label: paragraph_title
text: Flyweights

label: text
text: Pte. Edwards (R.S.) v. Pt Mabey (10). Edwards we knocked out in the first round.

label: text
text: Brazier (7). The fight opened with wild hitting on both sides, Baker taking the floor twice. and Brazier once. The latter with his longer reach had a slight advantage in the second round and swung lefts and rights, but Baker had piled up enough points at the end of the third round to be given the decision.

label: paragraph_title
text: Bantamweights.

label: text
text: Pte. Foster (R.S.) v. Drm. Simpson (D.S.). Simpson went at a fast pace and disposed of his opponent by a knockout in the first round.

label: text
text: Pte. Baxter (1) v: Pte. Dawson (4). The fighting throughout the three rounds was slow, with Baxter doing the attacking. Dawson crouched often and was at his opponent's mercy, but the latter was not inclined to take advantage. Baxter won.

label: text
text: Pte. Lleliott (1) v. Drm, Bowles (D.S.). Lleliott was floored three times in the first round, and in the next received a knockout. Bowles fought well and his blows proved to be hard and accurate.

label: text
text: Pte. Williamson (1) v. Pte. Key (4). This was an evenly matched pair and the fight went the full way. Key was forced to fight at close quarters and in this his opponent had the better of him. Williamson won.

label: text
text: L-C. Leavey (D.S.) v. Pte. Simmons (7). Simmons disposed of his opponent easily by the K.O. route with a right swing early in the first round.

label: text
text:
Middleweights.
Pte. Eaton (4) v. L.C. Wright (R.S.). Eaton did all the attacking, his opponent being content to back to the ropes where he got cornered and received a shower of blows. In the second and third rounds he received more punishment. Eaton won.
Pte. Problitts (1) v. Pte. Elliott (14). Problitts forced the fighting with left jabs following up in the next round with very effective
swinging blows which sent Elliott to his knees twice. The latter was a beaten man, but started well in the third round, only to be knocked out.

label: text
text:
Light-heavyweight.
Pte. Gravett (7) v. Pte. Williams (D.S.) Gravett won easily in the first round by knocking out his opponent with a series of heavy right swings on the neck. Williams hardly retaliated.

label: paragraph_title
text: FINALS.

label: paragraph_title
text: Flyweight.

label: text
text: Pte. Mabey (10). v. Drm. Baker (D.S.). This bout went the full way. Mabey had the advantage in reach, and Baker at first was content to keep on jabbing. His fighting improved later, although Mabey occasionally broke through his defence. Baker won.

label: paragraph_title
text: Bantamweight

label: text
text: Drm. Simpson (D.S.) v. Pte. Baxter (1). This was the best bout of the evening and the spectators were treated to a spirited fight. Simpson started by delivering a round of left and right swings, many of which, however, missed. In the second round there was hard hitting on both sides, Simpson receiving a cut below his right eye after he had done the like to his opponent in a lesser degree. Heavy blows were also exchanged in the third round. Baxter was given the decision.

label: paragraph_title
text: Featherweight.

label: text
text: Pte. Cooper (2 v. Drm. Bowles (D.S.)). Bowles started to chase his man round after he had floored him with a heavy right. Cooper had to be continually on his guard and by constantly attacking Bowles gained enough points to gain the decision.

label: paragraph_title
text: Lightweight.

label: text
text: Pte. Williamson (1) v. Private Simmons (7). With a heavy left early in the first round, Williamson sent his opponent to the floor for a knockout.

label: paragraph_title
text: Welterweight.

label: text
text: Pte. Mann (1) v. Pte. Pooley (3). The fight was given up by Pooley at the end of the second round as he had injured his arm. He was the aggressor, but there was hardly any forceful hitting. Middleweight.

label: text
text: Pte. Eaton (4) v. Pte. Problitts (1). In the first two rounds problitts did most of the attacking and seemingly tired himself in chasing his opponent round the ring. The blows created little impression on Eaton, who fought smilingly. In the third round Eaton tried to clinch matters by rushing, but they were both soon exhausted and were hardly able to strike. Problitts won.

label: paragraph_title
text: Light-heavyweight.

label: text
text: Pte. Gravett (7). v. L.-C. Brand (R.S.). Gravett started the pace with heavy right swings, but soon found himself placed on his guard with his opponent getting the better of him in the exchanges. Dodging very neatly the swings sent in his direction, Brand got home some powerful lefts in the second round, following up with a variety of right and left swings and straights. Gravett fought gamely. Brand won.

label: paragraph_title
text: LADIES' GOLF

label: text
text: After several months' absence from the game through illness, Miss Cecil Leitch returned to competitive golf when at Moor Park the annual tournament among the Medical, Legal, Parliamentary, and United Services ladies' golfing associations was decided.

label: paragraph_title
text: LLNESSEOYER

label: vision_footnote
text: Miss Cecl Leitch

label: text
text: Miss Leitch led the first named association, who secured the trophy in 1928 and 1924, but, although she won both her games and her side was successful in the semi-final against the Parliamentary team, United Services took the shield by defeating Medical in the afternoon by 7 games to 2. A feature of the morning play, when Medical beat Parliamentary by 7 to 1 (a player being absent from either side), and United Services beat Legal by 5 to 4, was the contrast in the short game of the two sisters, Miss Cecil and Miss Edith Leitch. Both were on the side of the Medicals, and whereas the ex-champion wouther games by most accurate putting Miss Edith Leitch could do little that was right on the greens, and lost to Mrs. E. Martin Smith by 2 and 1.

label: paragraph_title

label: text
text: Except in the most important race of the day, good fields were sent out for the various events of the card on Saturday—the first day of the Whitsuntide extra meeting which continues this afternoon.

label: text
text: A drizzle now and then did not dampen the enthusiasm of the spectators who attended.

label: text
text:
Racing honours were evenly distributed but Mr. Pollock rode three winners in five attempts.
H.E. the Governor (Sir R. E. Stubbs): accompanied by his A.D.C. (Captain R. Neville, R.M.L.I.) and Private Secretary (Mr. T. J. Galsford St. Lawrence) arrived in time to led in his pony, Gaudie, which ran third in the opening event; this race was won by Lady Severn's Jambu (the griffin's second victory) and the Hon. Sir Claud Severn was also present.

label: text
text: It is interesting to note that Hailsham, who finished between Jambu and Gaudie, was once the property of Captain Neville. The A.D.C.'s entry, Valiant, was unplaced in the same event. In the sixth race Gaudie was placed second and Valiant third. Langsat, another of Lady Severn's ponies, was backed in preference to either Gaudie or Valiant, but was unplaced.
